## Open questions

- **Deployment target.** The ADR (Proposed, 2026-10-05) puts the work on Azure (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage). It is background, not an accepted choice. Only Stage 6 depends on the answer, so it can wait until Stage 6's brainstorming session.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Filing-index table
      Objective: Build one filing-index table from real quarterly and daily master index files.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a local filing-index table whose rows carry each filing's archive path; `specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md`
      Exit: the table exists, built from real SEC quarterly and daily indexes over the range chosen in the stage's session. The findings file records files fetched, bytes, row count, wall time and observed request rate.
      Leaves out: source-state manifest, raw-byte replay, quarterly reconciliation and withdrawal gating, versioned per-quarter publication (Stage 4); scheduling, deployment and monitoring (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submission download (bounded slice)
      Objective: Download the submissions that a bounded slice of index rows names.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: submissions on local disk for the slice, keyed to their index rows; `specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-2-findings.md`
      Exit: every row in the slice has its submission on disk or a recorded failure. The findings file records files, bytes, wall time and request rate, and projects the full-history download from those figures.
      Leaves out: full-history campaign with resume across runs and one shared request budget (Stage 5); scheduling and deployment (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick 10-K and 8-K filings out of the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's submissions on disk
      Produces: extracted main documents for the slice's 10-K and 8-K filings, linked to their index rows; `specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-3-findings.md`
      Exit: every 10-K and 8-K in Stage 2's slice has an extracted main document or a recorded reason it has none. The findings file records counts, failures and processing time.
      Leaves out: running over the full history (Stage 5); scheduling and deployment (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Index hardening
      Objective: Bring the filing-index table to a resumable, replayable, reconciled standard.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 1's table and findings
      Produces: per-source state; retained raw index bytes with replay; quarterly reconciliation; versioned per-quarter publication (background spec §4.2 and §4.4–4.6 as candidate contracts)
      Exit: an interrupted ingest resumes without re-fetching completed sources. A parser change rebuilds the table from stored bytes with no SEC requests. A changed quarterly file publishes a new generation with a change report, and any removal waits on approval.
      Leaves out: scheduling, deployment and monitoring (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Full-history submissions
      Objective: Download and handle submissions across the full requested history.
      Outcomes: O2, O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's and Stage 3's findings (projected cost); Stage 4's per-source state
      Produces: the full requested history of submissions, and their 10-K/8-K main documents, with durable progress
      Exit: every index row in the requested range has its submission on disk or a recorded failure, and every 10-K/8-K among them has its main document extracted. The findings file records measured totals and the rate held throughout.
      Leaves out: scheduling, deployment and monitoring (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Scheduled operation
      Objective: Run daily ingestion and periodic reconciliation unattended on the chosen platform.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 4 and 5; the answer to the deployment-target open question
      Produces: deployed, scheduled runs with monitoring, alerts and runbooks
      Exit: scheduled daily runs catch up after a missed run without losing older work, and their durable reports and alerts show it. Reconciliation has run on its schedule at least once.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming
